title: Reward-free Pretraining for Reinforcement Learning via Occupancy Coverage Maximization
claim: Without a sink mechanism, coverage collapses and oscillates over earlier regions; with it, exploration expands while retaining earlier coverage.
layout: 2 rows by 5 columns of heatmaps, left-to-right time arrow
description: The figure is a 2×5 grid of grid-world heatmaps. Rows are labeled 'w/o sink' (top) and 'w sink' (bottom). Columns show successive policy-optimization rounds, with a long black arrow labeled 't' running left to right underneath. Each heatmap shows a multi-room corridor of 24 columns by 6 rows. Gray T-shaped walls divide the rooms, and visited cells are colored on a log-scale viridis colorbar at the right (yellow is high count, dark purple is low). In the top row, coverage stays confined to the first rooms and shifts around, leaving earlier cells dark or empty. In the bottom row, the colored region grows steadily across the rooms until it spans nearly the whole corridor. The eye goes first to the bright yellow patches at the left and to the widening coverage in the bottom row.
caption: Effect of sink-state augmentation under an intentionally severe zero-buffer update in the multi-room environment. Each column shows a later policy-optimization round, with visitation counts plotted on a log scale. Top: without the sink state, the learned operator is fit only to the most recent batch, so previously covered regions become unsupported and the policy oscillates over the first rooms. Bottom: with the sink state, unsupported mass is routed to a controlled absorbing state, yielding policies that expand while retaining connected coverage of earlier regions.
abstract: Sparse rewards pose a central challenge in reinforcement learning, since agents receive no informative signal until they reach their goal. Intrinsic-reward methods address this issue by optimizing non-stationary objectives such as novelty, prediction error, or skill diversity, thereby injecting a supervision signal into the problem. While effective, these methods often require that the extrinsic (sparse) reward can be evaluated -- either online or during offline relabeling of the stored transitions. This limitation is particularly vexing for multi-task, meta-, and continual reinforcement learning, where agents' interactions with the environment are usually reward-free. In this work, we present a method to pre-train transferable exploration policies that rapidly adapt to sparse rewards at downstream task time. Our objective maximizes state-space covering for the occupancy measure, and can be framed in terms of entropy maximization. Its algorithmic implementation, ROVER, leverages recent advances on the operatorial formulation of RL to estimate occupancy with a learned resolvent world model, bypassing common hurdles associated with density and entropy estimation. ROVER further introduces a virtual "sink" state for unexplored regions, balancing coverage of known states with expansion into unseen ones and preventing cyclic expansion-collapse behavior during learning. In tabular and pixel-based sparse navigation tasks, ROVER produces more uniform aggregate coverage and stronger initializations for downstream tasks than standard reward-free baselines.
